title: Ordinary Hom calculation for bounded finite-projective complexes on a ringed site
statement: Let (C,J,R) be a small ringed site with commutative coefficient sheaf and the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let E be a bounded cochain complex of module sheaves with a degreewise finite-free retract package [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Write O for the coefficient complex in degree zero and D=Hom-complex(E,O) [def-pur-hom-complex]. Then D is bounded and admits a finite-free retract package, and ordinary Hom out of E and D sends the fixed K-injective augmentation to a quasi-isomorphism (for arbitrary target complexes for E and for O for D). The actual ordinary signed bidual E to Hom-complex(D,O) and every actual ordinary evaluation Tot(F tensor D) to Hom-complex(E,F), characterized in [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], are isomorphisms of complexes.

source.place: Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect; Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, bounded strictly perfect calculation in the final two paragraphs.

proof.text:
For any term $T=E^i$, choose its splitting $T\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{p}T$. With the standard sections $u_j$ and coordinate functionals $u_j^*$ put $t_j=p(u_j)$ and $\lambda_j=u_j^*i$, so $\sum_jt_j\lambda_j=1_T$. The sheaf Hom and tensor definitions [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] give, for every module sheaf $B$, mutually inverse maps
$$B\otimes T^\vee\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom(T,B),\quad b\otimes\phi\longmapsto(t\mapsto b\phi(t)),\qquad h\longmapsto\sum_jh(t_j)\otimes\lambda_j.$$
Indeed their composites send $h$ to $h\sum_jt_j\lambda_j=h$ and $b\otimes\phi$ to $b\otimes\sum_j\phi(t_j)\lambda_j=b\otimes\phi$. All formulas are compatible with further restriction. The dual maps $p^\vee,i^\vee$ exhibit $T^\vee$ as a summand of $(\mathcal O^{\oplus r})^\vee=\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$. The double-dual map $t\mapsto(\phi\mapsto\phi(t))$ has inverse $\alpha\mapsto\sum_j\alpha(\lambda_j)t_j$. Finally $\mathcal Hom(T,-)$ is a retract, naturally in its argument, of $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O^{\oplus r},-)=(-)^{\oplus r}$. The latter is exact by [lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact]. Applying the retraction to any short exact sequence splits its kernels, images and cokernels, so its retract sequence is exact too.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, final finite-free/direct-summand calculation; dual splittings and termwise evaluation

proof.text: For the fixed K-injective augmentation F to I(F), Hom(E^i,-) is exact by step 1. The bounded exact-source Hom calculation [lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso] therefore gives a quasi-isomorphism Hom-complex(E,F) to Hom-complex(E,I(F)). Equivalently, filter by the finitely many source degrees of E: the successive quotients are shifted exact termwise Hom functors, so induction and the cohomology long exact sequence apply to arbitrary unbounded F. This finite filtration proof works with independent site and coefficient universes; no exactness of infinite products is used.

source.place: Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect, ordinary-to-derived Hom comparison; bounded exact-source proof instead of its local-actual-map argument

proof.text: The Hom-product description [def-pur-hom-complex] and the fact that O is concentrated in degree zero identify D^q with Hom(E^(-q),O), and d_D^q with (-1)^(q+1) times the dual of d_E^(-q-1). If E is supported in [a,b], then D is supported in [-b,-a]. Step 1 dualizes the chosen finite-free retractions, producing a finite-free retract package for D. Step 2 applied to D gives its augmentation comparison at O.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, second paragraph, model of the dual and finite-free-summand dual terms

proof.text: For the ordinary signed bidual map characterized in [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], the Hom-product projections identify its degree-i component with (-1)^i times termwise double-dual evaluation. The dual basis identity of step 1 gives the inverse, including for odd i and in characteristic two. This proves invertibility as an actual chain map, not merely of its localization.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, second paragraph: canonical bidual map is termwise evaluation up to sign; Tag 0A97 for the canonical map

proof.text: In degree n, the ordinary evaluation of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] is the finite sum, over p+q=n, of F^p tensor (E^(-q))^dual to Hom(E^(-q),F^p), y tensor phi mapping to (x mapping to phi(x)y). The dual basis inverse of step 1 inverts every summand; both sides have the same finite indexing because E is bounded. Expanding the differentials gives d_F y tensor phi + (-1)^(p+q+1)y tensor (phi d_E) on the tensor side, exactly d_F f-(-1)^n f d_E on the Hom side. Thus the componentwise inverse is an inverse chain map. The formula also covers zero ranks, the zero ring and unbounded F.

theorem ringedSiteStrictPerfectHom
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      ((sheafCompose J
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R))]
    (E : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      ((sheafCompose J
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (hE : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (E.X n))
    (pE : SheafOfModules.StrictPerfectCoefficientPackageOnSite _ E) :
    let D := homComplex.{c, v, max c v r, max c v r} (R := R) E
      (ringedSiteDualityUnitComplex.{c, v, r} J R)
    (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (D.X n)) ∧
    Nonempty (SheafOfModules.StrictPerfectCoefficientPackageOnSite _ D) ∧
    (∀ F, QuasiIso (ringedSiteHomComplexMap.{c, v, r} J R (𝟙 E)
      ((ringedSiteHomAugmentation.{c, v, r} J R).app F))) ∧
    QuasiIso (ringedSiteHomComplexMap.{c, v, r} J R (𝟙 D)
      ((ringedSiteHomAugmentation.{c, v, r} J R).app
        (ringedSiteDualityUnitComplex.{c, v, r} J R))) ∧
    IsIso (ringedSiteOrdinaryBidual.{c, v, r} J R E) ∧
    (∀ F, IsIso (ringedSiteOrdinaryEvaluation.{c, v, r} J R E F))
